tagline: International representation for European inland waterway transport since 1877
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of participants in the annual congress (225 in 2024, from 11 European countries) reflects the influence and international reach of the IVR as a major representative body of the European inland waterway sector. This metric demonstrates the active engagement of members and stakeholders in the association's governance.

kpis.name: Annual Congress Participants
kpis.explanation: Number of participants in the IVR annual congress, reflecting the organization's engagement and international reach.
kpis.description: The IVR annual congress (May 15-17, 2024 in Frankfurt) gathered 225 participants from 11 European countries, including sessions of the board of directors, general assembly, and technical committees.
kpis.signal: 225 participants from 11 European countries at the Frankfurt 2024 congress, demonstrating IVR's pan-European influence.

kpis.name: Loss Prevention Colloquium Participants
kpis.explanation: Number of participants in the first loss prevention colloquium organized by the IVR in Antwerp.
kpis.description: On November 4, 2024, the IVR organized its inaugural loss prevention colloquium in Antwerp, gathering approximately 80 professionals (insurers, brokers, maritime experts, lawyers) for eight presentations on technical and financial aspects.
kpis.signal: Successful inaugural edition with 80 participants from Belgium, Netherlands, and Germany, creating a new exchange platform.

kpis.name: Member Countries Represented
kpis.explanation: Number of European countries represented at the IVR annual congress.
kpis.description: The IVR represents the interests of European inland navigation with confirmed presence from 11 European countries at the 2024 congress.
kpis.signal: Pan-European presence with 11 countries represented at the 2024 congress, confirming the IVR's international role.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or advanced automation technologies in the 2024 annual report.
evidence: The report focuses exclusively on regulatory, technical, and organizational aspects of European inland navigation
Discussions address decarbonization, CESNI standards, safety, and loss prevention without reference to AI
Digitalization is mentioned in the context of CESNI standards but without details on specific AI technologies
